what_happened: The job to add a self-queued fix backlog line to `athena status` was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier gave one blocker and one major finding. The blocker: the count only covers requests queued on the "steward" channel, but Hestia queues its own requests on the "cli" channel (hestia.rs and reading.rs), so Hestia's self-queued requests are not counted. The major finding: the doc comment in status.rs and the CHANGELOG entry say Hestia uses the steward channel, and the code contradicts this. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks.
cause: The measure's selection rule was written from an assumption about which channel each self-queuing agent uses. Nothing made the producer find every code path that queues self-originated requests, or check the filter value against the real writers, before the doc comment and changelog were written. The same unverified assumption was copied into the doc and changelog. Only the verifier's reading of the code found the mismatch. This is the same kind of gap as the inventory job that listed a proxy set instead of the full defined surface. In both, a measure counts a subset and passes its own checks.
other_causes: The reading and criteria asked for a count of self-queued requests but did not name every queuing source, so the 'steward' channel could look sufficient.
The tests probably used fixtures with steward-channel entries only, so the missing source had no failing case.
open_hypotheses: The fields given do not show whether the reading named the steward channel explicitly or the producer chose it.
The fields do not show whether the tests used fixtures with cli-channel Hestia entries.
contradictions: The earlier case 20261113-050222-w50q is a similar proxy-set gap, but it concerned an inventory over files, not a channel filter in a status measure, so the match is partial.
prevention: Add a default for jobs that add a counting or status measure. Before the producer writes the selection filter, it must list every code path that writes the counted records. It must cite the real field values those paths use, and the tests must include one fixture entry from each writer. The doc comment and changelog may state only what that list shows. This covers the whole class of measures that count only the source they were handed.
proposed_request: Add a line to `athena status` that counts self-queued fix requests, meaning requests Athena's own agents queued rather than a person. First find every code path that queues such requests. This includes the steward and Hestia, which queues on channel "cli", and any others found in crates/athena-core (for example hestia.rs and reading.rs). Count requests from all of them, using the channel or marker value each one actually writes. Acceptance: (1) the status line counts self-queued requests from every path found; (2) a test has one fixture entry per path, including a Hestia entry on the cli channel, and checks each is counted while a request queued by a person is not; (3) the doc comment and the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry describe the counted sources exactly as the code does; (4) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test pass; (5) the report cites the commands run, per D43.
